title: A failed resolution leaves go.mod and go.sum as they were
when: With a project with applied code, go.mod and go.sum, and a fake go runner: Resolution fails in nine ways: the tidy, verify, list and diff commands; a source file added, edited or deleted during the run; go.mod edited during the run; and cancellation.
then: go.mod and go.sum keep their bytes each time, and no transaction file is left.
notes: Not proof yet: the interrupted case (TestDependencyRecoveryCompletesBothModuleFiles) checks that recovery succeeds, not that both files are then exactly the old or exactly the new version.

title: A saved overlay flag and ambient GOFLAGS cannot change what resolution reads
when: With a project with applied code, a Go configuration file that saves a -overlay flag naming another import, an invalid ambient GOFLAGS, and the local Go SDK offline: Resolution runs.
then: The overlay's import never reaches go.mod, and the source is unchanged.
notes: It covers the example the invariant names, a saved -overlay flag, plus ambient GOFLAGS and a GOWORK that points nowhere (ST-BLD-UC01-R02-T02). A real go.work or -modfile is not exercised.

title: An offline record names a cache and no proxy, and an online record names no cache
when: With a valid offline build record and a valid online one: The offline record is given a proxy, a missing cache inventory or a cache of zero files; the online record is given a cache.
then: validateRecord refuses each.
notes: Not proof yet: it checks the record's shape, not a build. Proof needs a build from a recorded cache with the network off that fails on a missing or mismatched module.

title: A build refuses an SDK that is not the verified one
when: With build options naming a fake go binary: Build runs.
then: It refuses the SDK and writes no work directory.
notes: Not proof yet: the pin is the compiler's sdkIdentity constant, not the archetype's; the archetype pin is not built (ST-SUP-INV08). Accepting the right SDK needs the real SDK.

title: A record whose inputs, modules or build settings changed is refused
when: With a valid build record: One thing changes: an input digest, the input order, the modules removed, a replacement path outside the source, an extra build flag, an ambient GOFLAGS, or a target that escapes.
then: validateRecord refuses each.
notes: Not proof yet: it shows the record's shape is enforced, not that Build writes a record naming every input. SBOM digests are not in the record (ST-BLD-DS01 is not built).

title: An image takes only a CA bundle of CA certificates
when: With cA bundles that are empty, a private key, a leaf certificate, surrounded by text, more than 512 certificates, or malformed: The trust store is read.
then: Each is refused.
notes: Not proof yet: BuildImage refusing an executable no trusted record names, the CA digest trust check, and never reading the host's trust store are not exercised.

title: Both records are checked against the exact signer identity before any output exists
when: With a consumer policy with an exact certificate identity, OIDC issuer and signer digest, and a mocked gh: The record check runs.
then: build.json and image.json are each checked with the exact identity, the issuer, the signer digest and --deny-self-hosted-runners, before any output exists, and the records are marked authenticated.
notes: Not proof yet: it checks the CI records' attestations with gh mocked, not an image signature; there is no keyless cosign signing, no SBOM attestation and no Tekton Chains key (ST-BLD-CMD05 is not built).

title: The same build gives the same image, running as non-root
when: With one executable and one CA bundle: The image is assembled twice, in two different directories.
then: Both records are equal and both OCI layouts have the same digests; the config runs as user 65532, with entrypoint /service and SSL_CERT_FILE set.
notes: It calls assembleImage, the whole of what stego image build writes after its checks.

title: A declaration without exactly one archetype is refused
when: With a declaration that names an archetype the registry does not hold: validate it.
then: The check reports an archetype fault that names the missing archetype.
notes: Covers only a missing archetype; a declaration with no archetype or two is not tested yet.

title: A declaration that carries an undeclared field is refused
when: With a declaration that carries a misspelled field at the root, in an entity field, in a collection or in a slot binding: parse it.
then: The parser refuses the declaration with an error that names the unknown field, the file and the line.

title: A declaration must be one document with no anchors, aliases or merge keys
when: With a declaration that holds a second document, an empty second document, an anchor or a merge key: parse it.
then: The parser refuses the declaration with an error that names the fault, the file and the line.

title: A declaration beyond 4 MiB or 128 levels is refused
when: Decode a declaration one byte over 4 MiB, decode a declaration nested 130 levels deep, and parse a file one byte over 4 MiB.
then: Each is refused, and the errors name the nesting limit and the byte limit.

title: A repeated entity name is refused
when: With a declaration that defines the same entity name twice: validate it.
then: The check reports an entity fault that says the entity is defined more than once.

title: A repeated field name in one entity is refused
when: With a declaration whose entity has two fields with the same name: validate it.
then: The check reports a field fault that names the entity and the repeated field name.

title: A field's constraints must suit its type
when: With a declaration whose fields carry constraints that do not suit their types, such as a length limit on a number, a numeric bound on a string, a pattern on a boolean, enum values on a string and a reference target on a string: validate it.
then: The check reports one field fault for each unsuitable constraint, and each fault names the constraint and the field type.

title: A repeated collection name is refused
when: With a declaration that defines the same collection name twice: validate it.
then: Validation stops with an error that names the duplicate key and the file line of the second definition.

title: A collection that names an undeclared entity is refused
when: With a declaration whose collection names an entity the declaration does not define: validate it.
then: The check reports a collection fault that names the missing entity.

title: A binding to an undeclared slot is refused
when: With a declaration that binds a policy fill to a slot no component declares: validate it.
then: The check reports a slot fault that names the unknown slot.

title: A binding to a slot no generator invokes is refused
when: With a registry component that declares a slot no registered generator consumes, and a declaration that binds a fill to that slot: validate it.
then: The check reports a slot fault that says no resolved generator consumes the slot.

title: A setting must match its component schema
when: Check setting values against component schema fields of each kind: string, boolean, integer, number, enum, optional, list of strings and list of objects, with both correct and wrong values.
then: Each correct value passes, and each wrong value gets an error that names the type mismatch, the unknown choice, the null, the wrong list item or the unknown or missing nested key.

title: An installation refuses an existing result folder and keeps what it holds
when: With a result folder that already holds a file: Installation runs into that folder.
then: Installation fails, the file keeps its content, and no download starts.

title: A changed asset or a failed signature leaves no installation
when: With a published release: One asset's bytes change, or a signature check fails, and installation runs.
then: Installation fails, and no result folder and no temporary download remain.

title: Recovery completes an interrupted apply, and plan and drift refuse until it does
when: With a project with applied output and a new plan: Apply stops at each journal point in turn.
then: Plan and drift refuse while the journal is pending. After recovery the output matches the record and no drift remains.

title: A record whose input manifest disagrees with it is refused
when: With a record with an input manifest: The manifest's declaration digest or registry reference differs from the record's.
then: STEGO refuses the record.

title: Apply refuses a plan whose registry content digest differs from the registry it reads
when: With a plan from a loaded registry: The registry content digest in the plan is replaced and apply runs.
then: Apply fails with a registry error and writes no output.

title: Apply refuses a plan that carries another compiler build
when: With a project applied by the current compiler: The compiler build in the plan is changed and apply runs.
then: Apply fails with a compiler error and leaves the record unchanged.

title: Apply refuses a plan when an input, the record or a generated file changed after planning
when: With a project with applied output and a fresh plan: One of service.yaml, go.mod, go.sum, the record, the config or a generated file changes, and apply runs.
then: Apply refuses the stale plan, and the changed file and the record keep their content.

title: A generator that emits one path twice stops planning
when: With a project whose generator returns the same output path twice: Planning runs.
then: Planning stops with a duplicate path error that names the path, and no plan is made.
notes: Two components cannot claim one path, because overlapping namespaces are refused before generators run. This test covers the remaining case, one generator that returns a path twice. The same check in reconciler.go also covers the slot and assembler files, because they join the list before the check runs.

title: A generator file outside its component namespace stops planning
when: With a component that declares an output namespace, and a generator that returns a file outside it: Planning runs.
then: Planning stops with a namespace error.
notes: TestReconcile_NoNamespaceComponentProducingFilesRejected covers the second clause, a component that generates files with no namespace, but has no ID of its own; the one test record names the first case.

title: A plan that writes, deletes or records a path outside the output folder is refused before a fill changes
when: With a project with a hand-written fill, and a plan that names ../fills/policy.go as a file to write, to delete or to record: Apply runs the plan.
then: Apply refuses the plan, the fill keeps its content, and the output folder is not created.
notes: TestApplyRejectsReservedOutputRoots shows the other half: an output folder set to fills, .stego, go.mod or service.yaml is refused.

title: A failed validation, generator or assembly leaves the output and the record unchanged
when: With a project with applied output and a record: A run fails in validation (a missing generator), in a generator (it returns an error) or in the assembler (a circular constructor dependency).
then: The run returns that error, and every file in the project keeps its content.
notes: No saved plan exists yet, so the test cannot show that a failed run saves no plan.
